$comment: The single source of truth for watchdog diagnostic texts, shared by the compiler plugin and
the documentation website.
Consumers:
- :kotlin-library-api-watchdog-compiler-plugin generates WatchdogDiagnosticMessages from this file (see its
build.gradle.kts). The generator appends a final 'See more: <docsBaseUrl><docs>' section
to every message, after messageTrailer if present, and escapes ' as '' for messages with
parameters, which the compiler renders through java.text.MessageFormat.
- docs/plugins/diagnostics.mjs validates the '// !diag[/range/] DIAGNOSTIC_NAME [params]'
Code Hike annotations in docs samples. The docs Code component renders their underlines,
fills the message template parameters, and shows the resulting diagnostic tooltips.
Fields:
name    - the diagnostic name, matching the property in WatchdogDiagnostics.
title   - the H1 of the check page, shown in the docs tooltip.
docs    - the check page path under docsBaseUrl, without an extension.
message - the message template as source-wrapped lines. Consumers join adjacent lines with
spaces and preserve empty lines as paragraph breaks. Docs render it as Markdown. The
compiler uses the same text. Enclose every code reference in backticks.
Write ' as a single quote: the generator escapes it where MessageFormat needs it.
Do not spell out the documentation link. The generator derives it from docs.
messageTrailer - optional sentence appended to the message before the documentation link.
parameterValues - optional named values for long or reusable diagnostic parameters, using the
same source-wrapped line format as message. Values may have {0}, {1}, ...
placeholders. Compiler checkers resolve them through generated code. Docs
annotations use $name or $name(value) references.
Links in message, messageTrailer, and parameterValues are written as Markdown links,
[text](url). The docs render them as links. The generator rewrites them to 'text (url)'
so compiler output stays readable.

diagnostics.name: OPEN_API_WITHOUT_SUBCLASS_OPT_IN
diagnostics.title: Open API without subclass opt-in

classFix: Mark it with `@SubclassOptInRequired` to control external subclassing. Alternatively, make
interfaceFix: Mark it with `@SubclassOptInRequired` to control external subclassing.

message: The {0} `{1}` can be subclassed outside the library without restriction, so the library can no
longer add abstract members, change existing members' signatures, or tighten invariants without
breaking external subclasses. {2}
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyOpen` to the {0}.

diagnostics.name: SUBCLASS_OPT_IN_WITHOUT_MARKERS
diagnostics.title: Subclass opt-in without markers
message: `@SubclassOptInRequired` lists no marker classes, so any external class can subclass `{0}`
without opting in to anything, and the library keeps the evolution risk it meant to opt out of.
Pass at least one opt-in marker class with a description of why the subclassing is restricted.

diagnostics.name: EXHAUSTIVE_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Exhaustive public API

enumFix: To keep the set extensible, replace the enum with a regular class and named instances.
sealedFix: To keep the subtype set extensible, replace the sealed hierarchy with a non-sealed class or
interface and use `@SubclassOptInRequired` to control external subclassing.

message: The {0} `{1}` can be matched exhaustively by users (a `when` with no `else` branch), so adding {2}
later makes every such `when` stop compiling. {3}
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyExhaustive` to the {0}.

diagnostics.name: UNDOCUMENTED_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Undocumented public API

declarationDocumentation: Document the behavior users can rely on.
memberPropertyDocumentation: Document the behavior users can rely on. Add `KDoc` directly, or add an `@property` tag for
the property to the containing class's `KDoc`.
constructorPropertyDocumentation: Document the behavior users can rely on. Add `KDoc` directly, or add an `@property` or `@param`
tag for the property to the containing class's `KDoc`.

message: The {0} `{1}` is part of the public API but has no `KDoc`, so users can only guess the usage
contract from the implementation, and any later change risks breaking a usage nobody wrote down as
supported. {2}
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyUndocumented` directly to the undocumented
declaration.

diagnostics.name: FUNCTION_TYPE_ALIAS_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Function type aliases in public API
message: The type alias `{0}` abbreviates a function type. The alias is erased from the compiled API, and users
bind to the bare function type. The problem is that it can never grow members, default implementations, or
constraints later. Declare a `fun interface` instead to keep lambda ergonomics behind a stable
nominal type.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyFunctionTypeAlias` to the type alias.

diagnostics.name: DATA_CLASS_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Data classes in public API
message: The `data class` `{0}` bakes its constructor property list into the compiled API through the
generated `copy` and `componentN` functions and the constructor itself, so adding, removing, or
reordering a property later is a breaking change. Declare a regular class and implement
`equals`/`hashCode`/`toString` explicitly, or generate them with the
[Poko](https://github.com/drewhamilton/Poko) library.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyDataClass` to the class.

diagnostics.name: STATEFUL_CLASS_WITHOUT_EQUALS
diagnostics.title: Stateful classes without equals
message: The class `{0}` holds state - at least one property with a backing field - but neither declares nor
inherits an `equals` implementation, so comparisons use object identity instead of the class's
meaningful state. Override `equals` and `hashCode` together. {1} Alternatively, in IntelliJ IDEA
press `{2}` or choose `Code | Generate` to generate the methods.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyWithoutEquals` to the class, or apply
`@IntentionallyWithoutEqualsHashCodeOrToString` to acknowledge all three inherited implementations.

diagnostics.name: STATEFUL_CLASS_WITHOUT_HASH_CODE
diagnostics.title: Stateful classes without hashCode
message: The class `{0}` holds state - at least one property with a backing field - but neither declares nor
inherits a `hashCode` implementation, so hash-based collections use object identity instead of the
class's meaningful state. Override `equals` and `hashCode` together. {1} Alternatively, in IntelliJ
IDEA press `{2}` or choose `Code | Generate` to generate the methods.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyWithoutHashCode` to the class, or apply
`@IntentionallyWithoutEqualsHashCodeOrToString` to acknowledge all three inherited implementations.

diagnostics.name: STATEFUL_CLASS_WITHOUT_TO_STRING
diagnostics.title: Stateful classes without toString
message: The class `{0}` holds state - at least one property with a backing field - but neither declares nor
inherits a `toString` implementation, so instances render as the opaque class-name-with-hash-code
default and reveal nothing in logs and debugger output. Override `toString` to render the current
state. {1} Alternatively, in IntelliJ IDEA press `{2}` or choose `Code | Generate` to generate the
methods.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyWithoutToString` to the class, or apply
`@IntentionallyWithoutEqualsHashCodeOrToString` to acknowledge all three inherited implementations.

diagnostics.name: MUTABLE_COLLECTION_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Mutable collections in public API

returnTypeFix: Expose a read-only type instead (arrays count as mutable collections too), and hand out a
parameterFix: Accept a read-only type instead (arrays count as mutable collections too), and make a copy
typeParameterFix: Constrain the type parameter to a read-only collection type instead.

message: The {0} `{1}` exposes the mutable collection type `{2}`. Once a mutable collection is shared across
the API boundary, it is unclear whether user-side and library-side mutations affect each other. {3}
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyMutableCollection` to the declaration,
parameter, or type usage.

diagnostics.name: PAIR_OR_TRIPLE_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Pair and Triple in public API
message: The {0} `{1}` exposes the tuple type `{2}`. Tuple components carry no domain meaning: at the use
site {3} and positional destructuring reveal nothing about the values, and the
fixed shape can't evolve - adding a value means switching to a different type, breaking users.
Declare a small class with descriptively named properties instead.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyPairOrTriple` to the declaration,
parameter, or type usage.

diagnostics.name: REQUIRED_PARAMETER_AFTER_OPTIONAL
diagnostics.title: Required parameters after optional ones
message: The parameter `{0}` of `{1}` is required but declared after an optional parameter, so it can't be
passed positionally without re-stating the defaults in front of it. Declare parameters from the
general to the specific: essential inputs first, optional inputs - defaulted and `vararg` parameters
- last. Move the required parameter in front of the optional ones.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyRequiredParameterAfterOptional` to the {2}.

diagnostics.name: INCONSISTENT_PARAMETER_ORDER_IN_OVERLOADS
diagnostics.title: Inconsistent parameter order in overloads
message: The parameters `{0}` and `{1}` of `{2}` appear in the opposite relative order in another overload.
Users transfer their expectations between overloads, so an inconsistent order of same-named
parameters invites silently swapped arguments that still compile. Keep shared parameters in the
same relative order across overloads.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyInconsistentParameterOrder` to the {3}.

diagnostics.name: BOOLEAN_PARAMETER_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Boolean parameters in public API
message: The function `{0}` takes the `Boolean` parameter `{1}`. At the call site a bare `true`/`false`
reveals nothing about its meaning, and users can't be forced to name the argument they pass.
Introduce separate, descriptively named functions for each mode, or replace the parameter with an
`enum class`.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyBooleanParameter` to the function or Boolean
parameter.

diagnostics.name: NULLABLE_BOOLEAN_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Nullable Booleans in public API
message: The {0} `{1}` exposes a nullable `Boolean`. `Boolean?` models three states but names only two of
them, so every use site has to know what `null` stands for, and three-state logic hides in
two-branch `if`s. Replace it with an `enum class` naming all three states, or drop the third state.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyNullableBoolean` to the declaration,
parameter, or type usage.

diagnostics.name: INLINE_FUNCTION_WITH_LOGIC
diagnostics.title: Inline functions with logic
message: The {0} `{1}` contains logic beyond a single thin delegating statement. The compiler copies an
`inline` body into every user binary, so logic placed there - and its bugs - stays frozen in users
compiled against an old library version until they recompile. Extract the logic into a function
without the `inline` modifier (`@PublishedApi internal` if it should stay out of the public API)
and delegate to it.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyInlinedLogic` to the declaration.

diagnostics.name: MANGLED_JVM_NAME_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Mangled JVM names in public API

functionFix: This mangles the JVM method name, so Java sources can't call it. Rename it with `@JvmName`,
or generate a Java-callable boxed variant with `@JvmExposeBoxed`.
nonFinalFunctionFix: This mangles the JVM method name, so Java sources can't call it. Open and abstract functions
support neither `@JvmName` nor a boxed variant from `@JvmExposeBoxed`, so change the signature
to avoid the value class if Java access is required.
propertyGetterFix: This mangles the getter's JVM name, so Java sources can't call the getter. Rename it with
`@get:JvmName`, or generate a Java-callable boxed variant with `@JvmExposeBoxed`.
propertySetterFix: This mangles the setter's JVM name, so Java sources can't call the setter. Rename it with
`@set:JvmName`, or generate a Java-callable boxed variant with `@JvmExposeBoxed`.
propertyGetterAndSetterFix: This mangles both accessors' JVM names, so Java sources can't call either accessor. Rename them
with `@get:JvmName` and `@set:JvmName`, or generate Java-callable boxed variants with
nonFinalPropertyGetterFix: This mangles the getter's JVM name, so Java sources can't call the getter. Open and abstract
properties support neither `@get:JvmName` nor a boxed getter from `@JvmExposeBoxed`, so change
the signature to avoid the value class if Java access is required.
nonFinalPropertySetterFix: This mangles the setter's JVM name, so Java sources can't call the setter. Open and abstract
properties support neither `@set:JvmName` nor a boxed setter from `@JvmExposeBoxed`, so change
the signature to avoid the value class if Java access is required.
nonFinalPropertyGetterAndSetterFix: This mangles both accessors' JVM names, so Java sources can't call either accessor. Open and
abstract properties support neither accessor `@JvmName` annotations nor boxed variants from
`@JvmExposeBoxed`, so change the signature to avoid the value class if Java access is required.
constructorFix: This hides the source constructor behind a synthetic one, so Java sources can't call it. Generate

message: The {0} `{1}` has the `value class` `{2}` in its signature. {3}
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyMangledJvmName` to the declaration or an
enclosing class.

diagnostics.name: KOTLIN_ONLY_API_WITHOUT_JVM_SYNTHETIC
diagnostics.title: Kotlin-only API without JvmSynthetic

suspend: is a `suspend` function, which Java sees with a trailing `Continuation` parameter it can't provide
reified: declares a `reified` type parameter, which only inlining Kotlin call sites can substitute - calling
the compiled method from Java fails at runtime
suspendFunctionType: takes a `suspend` function type in the parameter `{0}`, which a Java lambda can't implement
extensionFunctionType: takes a function type with receiver in the parameter `{0}`, which a Java lambda can only emulate by
taking the receiver as an explicit first argument
unitFunctionType: takes a `Unit`-returning function type in the parameter `{0}`, which forces a Java lambda to return

message: The function `{0}` {1}. Kotlin callers see the intended shape, but the function still lands in the
API surface Java sources see. Hide it from Java with `@JvmSynthetic`, or provide a Java-friendly
alternative.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyKotlinOnlyApi` to the function or an
enclosing class.

diagnostics.name: COMPANION_API_WITHOUT_JVM_STATIC
diagnostics.title: Companion function without JvmStatic
message: The `companion object` function `{1}` compiles to an instance method on the nested `{2}`
class, so Java callers have to reach it as `{0}.{2}.{1}(...)`. Mark it with `@JvmStatic` to
additionally compile a static `{0}.{1}(...)` entry point for Java callers - Kotlin call sites are
unaffected. Alternatively, hide it from Java with `@JvmSynthetic`.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyNonStaticCompanionApi` to the function or an
enclosing class.

diagnostics.name: COMPANION_PROPERTY_WITHOUT_STATIC_ACCESS
diagnostics.title: Companion property without static access

getterFix: Mark the property with `@JvmStatic` to add a static getter on `{0}`. To change only this accessor,
use `@get:JvmStatic` to expose it or `@get:JvmSynthetic` to hide it.
setterFix: Mark the property with `@JvmStatic` to add a static setter on `{0}`. To change only this accessor,
use `@set:JvmStatic` to expose it or `@set:JvmSynthetic` to hide it.
getterAndSetterFix: Mark the property with `@JvmStatic` to add static accessors on `{0}`. To change the accessors
independently, use `@get:JvmStatic`/`@set:JvmStatic` to expose them or

message: The `companion object` property `{1}` leaves its {2} on the nested companion class, so Java
callers have to use `{0}`. {3}
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyNonStaticCompanionApi` to the property or an
enclosing class.

diagnostics.name: TOP_LEVEL_API_WITHOUT_JVM_NAME
diagnostics.title: Top-level API without JvmName
message: The facade class `{0}` contains this file's {1}. Its name is derived from the file name: it reads as
an implementation detail at Java call sites, and renaming
the file - invisible to Kotlin callers - renames the facade and breaks Java callers. Choose and pin
the facade name deliberately with `@file:JvmName`.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@file:IntentionallyDefaultFacadeName` to the file.

diagnostics.name: DEFAULT_PARAMETERS_WITHOUT_JVM_OVERLOADS
diagnostics.title: Default parameters without JvmOverloads
message: The {0} `{1}` declares default parameter values, but for Java callers the defaults don't exist: only
the full signature is compiled, and every argument must be spelled out. Mark the {0} with
`@JvmOverloads` to generate overloads that omit trailing defaulted parameters.
If this API shape is intentional, apply `@IntentionallyWithoutJvmOverloads` to the {0}.

diagnostics.name: PUBLIC_TYPE_WITH_INTERNAL_API
diagnostics.title: Public types marked as internal API
message: The {0} `{1}` publicly exposes `{2}`, but that type is marked as internal API with `@{3}`. Keep the
internal type out of the public signature, or mark the exposing declaration with an internal API
annotation too.

diagnostics.name: PUBLIC_TYPE_FROM_NON_TRANSITIVE_DEPENDENCY
diagnostics.title: Public types from non-transitive dependencies
message: The {0} `{1}` publicly exposes `{2}`, but the dependency providing that type is not published
transitively to consumers. Declare the dependency with `api` instead of `implementation`.

diagnostics.name: EXEMPTION_WITHOUT_EXPLANATION
diagnostics.title: Exemptions without explanation
message: The `@{0}` exemption doesn't explain why it is applied: the `{1}` reason doesn't speak for itself,
and the `description` is empty, so the exemption records nothing for the next reader. Pass a
self-explanatory reason (`FOR_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBILITY`, `API_DESIGN`), or describe the motivation
in the `description` argument.

diagnostics.name: DSL_MARKER_NOOP_TARGET
diagnostics.title: DSL markers with no-op targets
message: The DSL marker `{0}` allows the `{1}` annotation target, but a DSL marker only takes effect on
classifier declarations (`CLASS`, `ANNOTATION_CLASS`), type usages (`TYPE`), and type aliases
(`TYPEALIAS`). Applied to a `{1}` element the marker restricts nothing and only gives a false sense
of receiver scope control. Remove the target from `@Target`.
If this API shape is intentional, apply
`@IntentionallyWrongDslMarkerTargetsForBackwardsCompatibility` to the DSL marker.

diagnostics.name: DSL_MARKER_WITHOUT_EXPLICIT_TARGETS
diagnostics.title: DSL markers without explicit targets
message: The DSL marker `{0}` declares no annotation targets, so it can't provide receiver scope control as
written. A missing `@Target` also defaults to ineffective targets while leaving effective type usage
(`TYPE`) and type alias (`TYPEALIAS`) targets unavailable. Declare `@Target(AnnotationTarget.CLASS,
AnnotationTarget.ANNOTATION_CLASS, AnnotationTarget.TYPE, AnnotationTarget.TYPEALIAS)` or a subset
of it.
If this API shape is intentional, apply
`@IntentionallyWrongDslMarkerTargetsForBackwardsCompatibility` to the DSL marker.

diagnostics.name: DSL_MARKER_NOOP_TYPE_POSITION
diagnostics.title: DSL markers on no-op type positions
message: The DSL marker `{0}` has no effect on this {1}: scope control only reacts to markers on the type of
an implicit value - a receiver type, a context parameter type, or a function type with such implicit
values. A named value is always accessed explicitly, so the marker restricts nothing here. Move it
to the class or to a receiver position, or remove it.
